E057-01.notes: Two independent clauses ('...stay out of public life' / 'she did all three'). A is a comma splice; B is a fused sentence; D is still a comma splice and adds a comma between subject and verb. C splits them with a period.

E057-02.notes: The relative pronoun is the subject of 'described', so 'who' is needed. A 'whom' is object case; C 'which' does not refer to people; D 'whose described' is ungrammatical because 'whose' needs a noun after it.

E057-03.notes: 'In the 1940s' and the past-tense narrative ('met', 'became', 'contained') call for simple past 'began'. A is present tense; B present perfect does not fit a specific past time; C future is illogical.

E057-04.notes: The subject is the singular 'Each one'; the participial phrase in between is meant to distract. B 'recreates' agrees. A, C 'are recreating' and D 'have recreated' are all plural forms.

E057-05.notes: A completes the parallel list of noun phrases concisely. B is illogical (being tiny would not make the labels readable) and leaves a clause hanging off a comma; C attaches an independent clause with only a comma; D is wordy and breaks the parallelism with 'and with labels to read'.

E057-06.notes: A, B and D all say the same thing twice (carefully/meticulously, closely/with care, closely/careful way). C is concise.

E057-07.notes: Sentence 11 says what the officers were asked to do in place of solving cases, which is a contrast, so 'Instead' fits. B is wrong because 11 is not an example; C is wrong because not being expected to solve does not cause the task; D is wrong because the sentences are not similar.

E057-08.notes: A state after a city takes commas on both sides, and the nonrestrictive 'where' clause needs a comma before it. A leaves out the comma after Maryland; B leaves out the comma between Baltimore and Maryland; C uses a semicolon before a dependent clause.

E057-09.notes: Sentence 7 gives specific examples that back up 'painstaking detail'. A is wrong because it adds new specifics instead of repeating; B is wrong because the cans are diorama details, not a turn to cooking; D is wrong because it says nothing about why that scale was chosen.

E057-10.notes: The essay shows how the dioramas taught officers to observe and says they are still used in training. A is false because the officers were not meant to solve the cases and Lee solved nothing; B misstates the focus, since family life is only sentence 1; C is contradicted by sentences 9-12.

E057-11.notes: A: 'which' would refer to 'greenhouses', so the sentence says the greenhouses failed (a vague or wrong antecedent). B: a semicolon cannot come before a dependent 'which' clause. C: a comma splice, and 'they' would mean the greenhouses or the engineers. D: 'an effort that' clearly names the sales attempt as what failed. (Sentence 5 'Neither...were' is an agreement error outside this item's underline.)
